texts.facts: This judgmentcumaward shall decide the claim petition of Mukesh Kumar filed under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "M.V. Act") as amended up to date to claim compensation for the injuries sustained by him in an accident caused by a Crane that took place on 25.08.2017. FIR No.570/17 u/ss 287/338 IPC was registered at Police Station Ranhola and chargesheet was filed against respondent No.1/Arun Kumar, driver of Hydra Ace Crane bearing registration No.HR51BP9160 (offending vehicle). 2. Copies of criminal proceedings including FIR, chargesheet, site plan etc. were filed by the petitioner. 3. Brief facts of the vehicular accident as averred in the claim petition are that at about 10:00 AM on 25.08.2017, petitioner Mukesh Kumar along with other workers was helping respondent No.1/driver of the offending Crane in lifting and shifting a cutter machine into factory. The driver of the offending Crane was driving the crane in a rash and negligent manner without taking safety precautions. Due to his negligent act, cutter machine fell down from the grip of the crane and fell over the right leg of the petitioner. Resultantly, petitioner sustained grievous injuries. He was removed to Rathi Hospital and then to AIIMS Trauma Centre for better treatment. 4. Subsequently, it transpired that the offending Crane was owned by respondent No.2/Makhan Lal Shah and insured with respondent No.3/ HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Ltd. 5. In the joint Written Statement filed on behalf of respondent Nos.1 and 2 i.e. driver and owner, it was averred that the accident took place solely due to negligence of petitioner as he was not vigilant while performing his duties at the site. It was also claimed that since the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent No.3/insurance company, hence, no liability can be fastened upon them. 3 6. In the Written Statement filed on behalf of respondent No.3/insurance company, it was claimed that the FIR was registered u/s 287/338 IPC and not u/s 279 IPC as respondent No.1/driver did not commit any offence due to rash and negligent driving. It was also averred that petitioner himself was responsible for sustaining injuries due to his own negligence. It was, however, admitted that the alleged offending vehicle was insured with it vide its Policy bear No.2316201832990500000 valid from 30.06.2017 to 29.06.2018. 7. In the Written Statement filed on behalf of respondent No.4/Santosh Gupta alleged to have hired the offending vehicle from respondent No.2/Makhan Lal Shah/Registered Owner , it was averred that at the time of accident, respondent No.4 was neither the registered owner nor the hirer of the alleged offending vehicle. It is was, thus, stated that no liability can be fastened upon him. 8. From the pleadings of the parties, contentions raised and material on record, the following issues were framed by this Tribunal vide order dated 03.07.2018: ISSUES: 1. Whether the petitioner Mukesh Kumar suffered grievous injuries in a Mukesh Kumar vs Arun Kumar on 22 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175597602/ 2 vehicular accident that took place on 25.08.2017 at about 10:00 AM at H.No.937, Gali No.15, Kotla Vihar, PhaseII, Ranhola, Najafgarh, Delhi involving a Hydra Ace Crane bearing registration No.HR51BP 9680, driven by respondent No.1/Arun Kumar, owned by respondent No.2/Makhan Lal and insured with respondent No.3/HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Ltd.? OPP 2. OPP 4 11. In a claim petition filed under u/s 166/140 of the M.V. Act, onus is on the claimant(s)/petitioner(s) to prove that he or she sustained injuries in a vehicular accident caused by the wrongful act or negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 12. In support of his claim, petitioner Mukesh Kumar examined himself as PW1; Ms.Shilpi Kushwaha, Prosthetist & Orthotist, P&O International Pvt.Ltd. as PW2 and Dr.Naresh Chandra, Specialist & HOD(Ortho), Guru Govind Singh Govt.Hospital as PW3. 13. In his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex.PW1/A), petitioner Mukesh Kumar (PW1) explained the mode and manner of the accident as described in para 3 of this award. 14. In his crossexamination by respondents, it was denied by petitioner Mukesh Kumar that he had sustained injuries due to his own negligence, inspite of the warning given by his employer Santosh Gupta. Rather, the incident was explained in detail by the petitioner PW1. It was testified by him that a heavy cutter machine was to be lifted with the help of the offending vehicle from outside the factory premises to inside the factory premises. In order to lift the machine, the clamping was done by the driver of the crane with the help of iron chains. He further testified that his employer/Santosh Gupta had directed him and 45 other employees to lift the machine with iron chains. When the machine was lifted at a height of about 8 feet, the cutter machine fell from the crane on the petitioner, inside the factory. PW1 placed on record Discharge Summary (Ex.PW1/14, colly), as per which, he was admitted to JPN Trauma Centre on 25.08.2017 and discharged on 02.09.2017 with diagnosis of "Crush injury right lower limb". Admittedly, the petitioner was treated at government hospital , petitioner is, thus, held entitled to a compensation of Rs.1,065/ (Rupees One Thousand and Sixty Five) under this head. 22. Petitioner is further awarded a compensation of Rs.50,000/ (Rupees Fifty Thousand) towards attendant charges. Loss of earning during the period of treatment 23.
texts.arguments: 15. The scrutiny of the testimony of PW1/Mukesh Kumar, petitioner, reflects that the cutter machine fell on him as the machine was not secured with the clamp properly by the driver of the crane. In his testimony, R1W1/Arun Kumar, driver of the crane admitted that at the time of the accident, it was he, who was Mukesh Kumar vs Arun Kumar on 22 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175597602/ 3 operating the offending crane. He also admitted that the machine was secured with iron chain by him with the help of 34 labourers. In RAJ KUMAR VS. AJAY KUMAR & ANOTHER (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases. The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. In a judgment titled as JAGDISH VS. MOHAN AND OTHERS, reported as 2018 ACJ 1011 delivered by three Judges Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court, the Hon'ble Supreme Court awarded compensation towards loss of future prospects in a case where the petitioner had sustained physical disability of 90% due to amputation of both his hands. Mukesh Kumar vs Arun Kumar on 22 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175597602/ 5 VS. CHAITANYA KUMAR BHARDWAJ, reported as 2019 I DELHI 494 and RELIANCE GENERAL INSURANCE CO.LTD. Since petitioner was aged 19 years at the time of the accident, hence, applying the criteria of multiplier laid down in SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER, (2009) 6 SUPREME COURT CASES 121, the multiplier applicable in this case would be 18 (eighteen). 31. In R.D. HATTANGADI VS. PEST CONTROL (INDIA) PVT.LTD., I (1995) ACC 281 (SC), where a road accident resulted in 100% disability due to paraplegia below waist to a lawyer (retired Judge), the Supreme Court observed as under: 9 Mukesh Kumar vs Arun Kumar on 22 January, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175597602/ 6 "That no amount of compensation can restore the physical frame of the appellant. It was very vehemently argued by learned counsel for insurance company that since Section 279 IPC was not invoked, it is evident that the accident had not taken place on a public way and therefore, no liability could be fastened upon insurance company. In a judgment titled as UNITED INDIA INSURANCE CO.LTD. VS. JAGAT & ORS. decided on 28.07.2017 in MAC.APP.55/2012 relied upon by the learned counsel for petitioner, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi had upheld the view of Learned Presiding Officer, MACT. The Learned Presiding Officer had relied upon judgments titled as National Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Abdul Khan @ Abdul Rashid Khan & Ors. {2006 (I) T.A.C. 756 (Cal)} and Ram Chandra & Anr. Vs. Shiva Narain & Ors. reported as IV (2006) ACC 838, wherein it was held that if a place is accessible to public, it is a public place even if it is a private property. In United India Insurance Co.Ltd. (supra), the accident had taken place in the compound of M/s Roadwings International Pvt.Ltd. which was a yard located in Tughlakabad. It was held that the accident spot cannot be considered as a private place for the reason that public was also allowed entry therein and that wherever public can enter with permission, the said place becomes a public place for the purpose of Motor Vehicle Act. 47. In order to avoid the compensation money being frittered away, balance amount of Rs.48,87,000/ (Rupees Forty Eight Lakh Eighty Seven Thousand) would be kept in FDRs in accordance with the order dt. 07.12.2018 passed by Hon'ble Mr.Justice J.R. Midha in RAJESH TYAGI & ORS. VS. JAIBIR SINGH & ORS. IN FAO NO.842/2003 as per details mentioned herein: "250 (two hundred fifty) fixed deposits of Rs.19,548/ (Rupees Nineteen Thousand Five Hundred & Forty Eight) each, in the name of claimant Mukesh Kumar, for the period of one month to 250 months respectively, with cumulative interest."
